description_en: Yangah Hiti takes its name from the locality known as "Yangah Tola." This historical monument houses various Licchavi-period artifacts and features three inscriptions from that era. Similar to otherhitisin the Kathmandu Valley, Yangah Hiti was constructed near a crossroad. However, contemporary developments have enclosed thehitiwith walls and private buildings, thus restricting access from the Yangah Tola crossroad.The stepwell, known ashitigāḥ, is structured with two levels of plinths decending to the base platform. Extending outward from the eastern wall of thehitigāḥare three spouts. The central spout, slightly larger than the other two, functions as the primary outlet. Positioned above each spout is a niche, with the central niche housing a statue of Umāmaheśvara. The niche above the southern spout contains a weathered stone statue of a deity, its features now obscured and beyond recognition.L. Bangdel1995, p. 206 mentions that one of these niches formerly contained a statue of Padmapāṇi Lokeśvara. Statues of Bhagīratha from the later medieval period are positioned beneath each spout, although they are scarcely discernible due to the inundation of the hiti. Originally, a jaḥdhuṃprotruded from the northern wall, but it has since collapsed and become overgrown with bushes. Numerous statues and artifacts from the Licchavi and later medieval periods have been excavated from thehiti. Among these discoveries, acaityaand anandībelong to the Licchavi period, while a statue of Śrīdhara Viṣṇu from the 12th century has also been identified (Pal1985, fig. 31). Similarly, upon examining photographs of the Bhagīratha statues now submerged, they likely originate from the later medieval period.The central spout features a complete figure of amakara, which, according to (S. KhanālaVS 2068, p. 150), is not seen anywhere else in the Kathmandu Valley. Typically, depictions ofmakarasonly portray their heads, but on this spout he is featured with a full body of a crocodile including a pair of limbs and a coiling tail.The presence of threesanadas from the Licchavi period in the form of inscriptions is another special feature at the Yaṅgāḥ Hiti. Although these inscriptions are not related to thehiti, they appear to have been placed there ashitis are frequented by the locals in their daily lives. The oldest of the three inscriptions dates back to the joint reign of King Bhīmārjunadeva and Jiṣṇugupta, circa 633 CE (D.Vajrācārya, VS 2030, p. 423). However, due to erosion, the text of this inscription cannot be accurately dated. Another inscription, dated Mānadeva Era 64 (640 CE), was installed during the joint reign of King Bhīmārjunadeva and Viṣṇugupta (D.Vajrācārya, VS 2030, p. 423 and p. 442). The inscription reveals that the statue of the reclining Viṣṇu in Buḍhānīlakaṇṭha, was  constructed by Viṣṇugupta. Another Licchavi inscription, dated Mānadeva Era 67 (643 CE), records the retention ofbirtālands by King Narendradeva in the name of Dakṣiṇakolīgrāma[1]draṅgathat was seized from the locals by Bhaumagupta (D.Vajrācārya, VS 2030, p. 463).see "Licchavi Kings according to three sources: https://asianart.com/articles/jaya/kings.htmlNo historical sources are available to provide a date for the initial construction of thehiti. Thehitihas undergone numerous renovations over the years, but unfortunately, the sponsor and exact dates of these renovations are not documented. The Department of Archaeology renovated thehitiin 2008-2009 CE (S. KhanālaVS 2068, p. 223). Within the decade following the renovation, the northern section of thehiticollapsed, and the rubble is yet to be cleared.The archaeologist Uddhava Ācārya believes that the original water source for thehitilies in the southern section of the city around the Lagana area. Two of the spouts used to flow continuously up until a decade ago (local knowledge, local resident, Maharjana, female, age 63). Presently, thehitihas run dry, although water still infiltrates from other sources, inundating thehitigāḥdue to a clogged drain. There are two drains in the east and north (S. KhanālaVS 2068, p. 223).At the time of documentation in 2021, thehitiwas overgrown by weeds, bushes, and partially submerged, thereby concealing numerous historically significant inscriptions and statues.[1]It is a Licchavi term that refers to the Kvaḥne (southern) area of present-day Kathmandu. The city was divided into two quarters back then: Dakṣiṇakolīgrāma and Kolīgrāma.Ṭolas like Lagana, Yaṅgāḥ, Brahmatvāḥ, etc. were known to be Dakṣiṇakolīgrāma. The central quarter of the city like Itum Bāhāḥ, Jana Bāhāḥ, etc. came under Kolīgrāma (Vajrācārya 1974: 90).
description_ne: यो हिति काठमाडौंको यङ्गाल टोलमा अवस्थित छ । लिच्छविकालीन तीन अभिलेख र सोही कालका कला सामग्रीहरू पाइने हिति भएकाले यसको खास महत्व रहँदै आएको छ । उपत्यकाका प्रायः हितिहरू दोबाटो, चौबाटो वा टोलहरू जोडिने सीमामा बनाइएको पाइन्छ । यसै प्रकार यो हितिको अवस्थिति पनि दोबाटोमै छ । यङ्गाल टोलको चोक वा दोबाटोमा अवस्थित भए तापनि वर्तमानमा हिति र दोबाटोको बीच पर्खाल एवं भवनहरू निर्माण भएकाले हितिको अस्तित्व छायामा परेको प्रतीत हुन्छ । सार्वजनिक हिति चौतर्फी संरचनाले घेरिएको परिसर (कम्पाउण्ड) भित्र पर्न गएको छ ।जमिनको सतहभन्दा दुई तहको पेटीमुनि (खाँचामुनि) पानी प्रवाह हुने तीन टुटीहरू स्थापना गरिएका छन् । तल्लो पूर्वी पेटीको अग्र भागमा तीनवटा ढुङ्गाका टुटीहरू हालिएका छन् जसमध्ये बीचको टुटी मुख्य हो र आकारमा पनि अन्य भन्दा केही ठुलो देखिन्छ । उत्तरी तल्लो पेटीमै गाभेर एक जःधुं पनि स्थापना गरिएको छ । हाल सो खण्ड भत्किएर झाडी उम्रिएको अवस्था भएकाले जःधुंको अत्तो-पत्तो नभएको अवस्था छ । तीनै टुटीहरूमाथि गवाक्ष बनाईएका छन् जसमध्ये मध्य टुटीमाथि उमामहेश्वरको मूर्ति स्थापित छ । दक्षिणतिरको टुटीमा निकै नै खण्डित अवस्थामा पुगेको मूर्ति छ जसको पहिचान गर्न गाह्रो छ । तीनमध्ये एकमाL. Bangdel1995, p. 206 ले १५ औं शदीको पद्मपाणि लोकेश्वरको मूर्ति भएको बताएका छन् तर हाल सो मूर्ति उक्त स्थानमा भेटिदैन । तीनै टुटीका तल्लो भागमा भगीरथको उत्तरमध्यकालीन मूर्ति रहेको छ तर हितिको सतह जलमग्न बनेकाले अहिले सो मूर्ति पनि लुप्त अवस्थामा छ । हितिमा लिच्छविदेखि उत्तरमध्यकालसम्मका विभिन्न मूर्तिहरू पाइएका छन् । यो पक्षले पनि यस हितिको महत्व बढेको छ । यहाँ भएकामध्ये चैत्य र नन्दीको प्रतिमा लिच्छविकालीन हुन् भने यहाँ प्राप्त श्रीधर विष्णुको मूर्तिलाईPal1985, fig. 31 ले १२ औं शदीको बताएका छन् । त्यसैगरी हितिमुनि राखिएको भगीरथको मूर्तिको कलाकारितालाई नियाल्दा उत्तरमध्यकालीन (१७ औं शदी) देखिन्छ ।यस हितिमा रहेका ढुङ्गेधाराहरूमध्ये बीचको टुटीमा मकरको मुखाकृतिको पछाडि गोहीकै आकृति निर्माण गरिएको छ । खुट्टा तथा गोलो आकारमा घुमेको पुच्छरसमेत निर्माण गरी मकरलाई पूर्ण रूप दिइएको छ । मकरको पूर्ण स्वरूपलाई टुटीमा कुँद्ने प्रचलन बिरलै पाइन्छ । उक्त ढुङ्गेधारा उपत्यकाका ढुङ्गेधाराहरूमध्येको एक विशिष्ट नमुनाका रूपमा रहेको छ जुन उपत्यकामा अन्त कतै पाइएको छैन (S. KhanālaVS 2068, p. 150) ।तीनवटा लिच्छविकालीन सनदपत्रहरू प्राप्त हुनु पनि यस हितिको अर्को महत्त्वपूर्ण पाटो हो । यी तीनै अभिलेखहरू हितिसंग सम्बन्धित नभई राज्यबाट भएका तत्कालीन निर्णयको सन्देश प्रसार गरिएका सनदपत्रहरू हुन् । लौकिक जीवनमा स्थानीयहरू अनिवार्य पुग्ने थलोको रूपमा हिति परिसर रहँदै आएको छ । यसर्थ लोकलाई प्रसार गर्नुपर्ने सन्देशयुक्त अभिलेखहरू हिति परिसरमा राखिएका थुप्रै उदाहरणहरू उपत्यकामा पाइन्छन् । यहाँ पाइएका तीनमध्ये भीमार्जुनदेव र जिष्णुगुप्तको संयुक्त शासनको बेला (हाल साल खिइसकेको) राखिएको अभिलेख सर्वप्रचीन हो भने पुनः भीमार्जुनदेव र विष्णुगुप्तको शासन अवधिमा राखिएको संवत् ६४ (सन् ६४०) को अभिलेख हितिमा पाइन्छ (D.Vajrācārya, VS 2030, p. 423 and p. 442) । यो अभिलेखले काठमाडौंस्थित प्रसिद्ध बुढानीलकण्ठ मूर्ति विष्णुगुप्तले नै स्थापना गरेका हुन् भनी पुष्टि गर्न मद्दत गर्दछ । त्यसैगरी अर्को अभिलेख संवत् ६७ (सन् ६४३) को हो जसमा भौमगुप्तले दक्षिणकोलीग्राम द्रंगबाट खोसेको विर्ता नरेन्द्रदेवले पुनः स्थापना गरिदिएको कुरा उल्लेख गरिएको छ (D.Vajrācārya, VS 2030, p. 463) ।अभिलेख्य प्रमाणको अभावका कारण हितिको निर्माण मिति एवं निर्माताबारे यकिन हुन सकेको छैन । तथापि हितिमा प्राप्त अभिलेख र लिच्छविकालीन कला-वस्तुहरूका आधारमा हिति लिच्छविकालमै अस्तित्वमा आइसकेको तथ्य ज्ञात हुन्छ । हितिमा १२ औं र १७ औं शदीतिर मूर्तिहरू थप्ने कार्य भएको पाइएबाट यसको पटक-पटक मर्मत एवं पुनःनिर्माण कार्य हुँदै आएको पनि सहजै अन्दाज गर्न सकिन्छ । अभिलेखीकरण गरिएको नपाइएकाले हिति कुन-कुन समयमा क-कसबाट जीर्णोद्धार गरिए भन्ने कुराको पनि निर्क्यौल गर्न सकिएको छैन । सन् २००८-२००९ मा पुरातत्त्व विभागले हितिको जीर्णोद्धार गरेको थियो (S. KhanālaVS 2068, p. 223) । उक्त जीर्णोद्धार कार्यले एक दशकको समयावधि पार गरे लगत्तै हितिको उत्तरी खण्ड पूर्णतः भत्की हिति परिसरमा इँट र माटो थुप्रिएको अवस्था छ ।पुरातत्त्वविद् उद्धव आचार्य दक्षिणबाट भूमिगत पानी प्रसार भएकोले यसको मूल दक्षिणतिर लगन क्षेत्रमा कतै रहेको बताउँछन् । त्यसैगरी पूर्व र उत्तरतिर गरी दुईतिरबाट निकास रहेको उनको भनाई छ (S. KhanālaVS 2068, p. 223) । वर्तमानमा मूलको उचित व्यवस्थापन नहुँदा टुटीबाट पानी प्रवाह हुन छाडेको छ । करिब एक दशक अघिसम्म यहाँका तीनमध्ये दुई हितिबाट निरन्तर पानी प्रवाह हुने गर्दथ्यो (local knowledge, local resident, Maharjna, female, age 63) । पानी टुटीबाट नभई अन्यत्र कतैबाट रसाएर निस्की हिति परिसर पुरै जलमग्न बनेको स्थिति छ । निकासको उचित व्यवस्था नहुँदा हितिमा जलाशयका साथै झार उम्रिएको छ । ऐतिहासिक महत्वका अभिलेख एवं मूर्तिहरू पानीभित्र पुरिएको दूरावस्थापूर्ण दृष्य देखिन्छ ।

historical_events.event_description: This inscription is not related to thehiti. Although the date of this inscription has already eroded, it is clear that it was installed during the joint rule of King Bhīmārjunadeva and Jiṣṇugupta. It declares the reduction of levies onmalla(a kind of pet animal) and their babies to facilitate the residents of Dakṣiṇakolīgrāma (D.Vajrācārya, VS 2030, p. 425).

This inscription is unrelated to thehiti.It was installed during the joint rule of King Bhīmārjunadeva and Viṣṇugupta, dated Mānadeva Samvat 64 (640 CE). It documents the rulers' pleasur with the efforts of people for having pulled a large stone for carving a statue of Viṣṇu. Viṣṇugupta granted the residents of Dakṣiṇakolīgrāma the privilege to wear jewelry, with the exception of anklets and armlets of specific kinds. The inscription also highlights Viṣṇugupta's commissioning of a large reclining statue of Viṣṇu in a pond at the base of the northern hills (Gopālarājavaṃśāvalīfol. 22). The inscription confirms what is recorded in the chronicle. Moreover, the inscription reveals a shift in Viṣṇugupta's approach toward justice. He showed leniency towards the residents of Dakṣiṇakolīgrāma concerning theft, murder, and crimes against the state. The decree in the inscription specifies that only the individual convicted of these crimes would face punishment, excluding their family members. This contrasts with the prevailing practice at the time, where even the family members of convicts were punished as accessories to the crime (D. Vajrācārya, VS 2030, p. 447).

This inscription is unrelated to thehiti. It records the retention ofbirtālands by King Narendradeva in the name of the residents of Dakṣiṇakolīgrāma. This retention is granted as a recognition of their service in caring for the temple of Māneśvara. The land was seized from them by Bhaumagupta (D. Vajrācārya, VS 2030, p. 467).
In 2008-2009, thehitiwas renovated by the Department of Archaeology.

In 2018 CE, in commemoration of the anniversary of their movement, the Save Nepa Valley group organized the cleaning of thehiti. Thehitihad been neglected, leading to an overgrowth of weeds and bushes, and the poor drainage system resulted in a flooded floor. The Nepal Army actively contributed to the cleaning initiative, and the deputy mayor of the Kathmandu Metropolitan City attended the program.
